notes: Taken from the Board of Elections' 46-day election notice, which lists every contest and issue with the precincts that vote on it. Issue wording is condensed from the notice; the full wording is on the sample ballot.

Candidates are listed alphabetically by last name, not in ballot order: Ohio rotates the order of names from precinct to precinct. Certified write-in candidates are not printed on the ballot and are not listed.

"Where you live" uses the state voter file: a district or school levy is shown for a city, village or township when any of its voters live in that district. Your exact ballot depends on your precinct.
The Board's notice does not give local issue numbers; see your sample ballot for them.

issues.jurisdiction: City of Columbus (Delaware, Fairfield and Franklin counties)
issues.title: Charter amendment (by petition): council members elected only by voters in their district
issues.text: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. Ballots within council districts would include both citywide races and the district race, and a recall election of a district council member could be started by a petition signed by district electors equal to at least 15% of the votes cast in the district in the preceding mayoral election. Shall the proposed charter amendment be approved?

issues.jurisdiction: City of Columbus (Delaware, Fairfield and Franklin counties)
issues.title: Charter amendment (by Council): district-only voting for district seats, at-large seats added, 13-member Council
issues.text: This proposed charter amendment would limit the ability to vote for candidates for Columbus City Council to only those electors living within the districts that those candidates seek to represent. It adds two at-large council members elected in 2027 and two more elected in 2029 (four-year terms), moving from a nine-member to an eleven- and then a thirteen-member Council; redraws the council district map in 2027 and raises the allowed population variance between districts from 1% to 7.5%; requires district candidates to have lived in their district for a year before the primary; updates expulsion, quorum and vote requirements; sets petition signature requirements (150 district / 250 at-large); and allows recall of district and at-large members by petition. Shall the proposed charter amendment be approved?

issues.title: Charter amendment: new Section 11.05 prohibiting construction of a data center
issues.text: Shall Article XI, Section 11.05 of the Charter of the City of Sunbury be adopted? It would prohibit the construction of a data center, defined as one or more buildings, facilities or infrastructure on a single parcel or on contiguous, adjacent or otherwise aggregated parcels used primarily or exclusively for digital information services (managing, storing, processing and disseminating electronic data with computer systems, servers, networking and related equipment, including cooling) with an aggregate monthly demand or peak load greater than 25 megawatts from any energy source. The section is self-executing.
